liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (6 reviews): Reviewer calls this Dark Star long, jazzy and intricate, and the opening of a favorite second-set suite; Quotes Deadbase calling this a thinking man's Dark Star, with cosmic jams and plenty of thematic interplay [9][11][12][13][16][19]
- **Eyes of the World** (2 reviews): Reviewer rates this Eyes among the band's best ever, possibly the very best; Jerry moves through several grooves in Eyes, which then melts into China Doll [9][16]
- **Mind Left Body Jam** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the jam blissful, in the middle of the Dark Star, Eyes, China Doll sequence; Reviewer calls it the most intense and focused version they have heard [9][12]
- **El Paso** (1 review): Reviewer hears this El Paso played with unusual intensity and passion, not as a throwaway [15]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-11.sbd.schlissel.14105.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 191 min; rated 4.86/5 by 43 [1]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.rolfe-miller.83318.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 191 min; rated 4.9/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: This source has more tuning before Dark Star and lacks the cut at the start of Eyes [2]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.pitch-corrected.miller.88485.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 190 min; rated 4.54/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Includes more tuning before Dark Star and no cut at the start of Eyes [3]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.gardner.12178.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 191 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [4]

## Around the show

- It was the last of three nights at Winterland, with Uncle John's Band and And We Bid You Goodnight as encores [11]
- Reviewer thinks this is likely the best 1973 Dark Star, though suggests also checking the 3/28 version [11]
- Reviewer ranks this Eyes alongside the top versions from 5/7/77 and 6/18/74 [12]
- Reviewer argues this could be the best show of 1973, with strong first-set material including Weather Report [16]
- Reviewer ranks this Dark Star first among all 1972-1974 versions, calling the comparison apples and oranges [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-11.sbd.schlissel.14105.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Disks 1-2 come from a master stereo recording, then cassette twice, DATs and CDRs; Tony Gardner used shntool to fix an earlier version of his own patched Eyes seed [1]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.rolfe-miller.83318.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D [2]. Also: Soundboard source via an unknown generation to DAT and CD; supplies a section of Eyes from DATs lent by Steve Rolfe [2]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.pitch-corrected.miller.88485.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D [3]. Also: Uses Steve Rolfe's DATs for the Eyes section; pitch corrected by 0.9% in Cool Edit Pro, with help from Rob Bertrando [3]
- **gd1973-11-11.sbd.gardner.12178.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Darrin Sacks and Tony Gardner; source: Disks 1-2 MSR>Cass>Cass>DATs>CDRs>EAC>SHN. Disk 3 MSR>Cass>DATs>CDRs>EAC>SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 11/11/73 Winterland Arena, San Fra…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27364594275/) [21]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27364594275/) [22]
